newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI COPPER FUTURES END MIXED IN SLOW TRADE.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI COPPER FUTURES END MIXED IN SLOW TRADE.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed in slow trade on Thursday due to uncertain short-term market direction after copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) failed to breach the $2,300 level overnight, traders said.
LME copper closed Wednesday at $2,298. It showed all the signs of remaining quiet and rangebound on Thursday, with comfort levels seen between $2,270 and $2,310 per tonne, London analysts said.
In Shanghai, the most actively traded December 1997 contract ended at 21,220 yuan ($2,560) per tonne, rising 20 yuan.
It opened at 20,250 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 21,300 and a low of 21,170 yuan per tonne.
August fell 50 to 20,650 yuan, September 190 to 20,800, October was unchanged at 21,100, November flat at 21,200, the January 1997 contract rose 200 to 21,200 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 17,720 tonnes from 25,320 tonnes.
Copper opened mixed and moved around opening levels for most of the session, with many investors remaining sidelined, traders said.
"Only retail investors were seen trading for quick profits today," one trader said.
"Most investors are waiting for clear direction from the LME," he said.
In Shanghai, physical copper prices were around 20,800 yuan, little changed from Wednesday's close due to consolidation on the futures market and slack spot consumption, traders said.
Traders said the LME would be an important influence on Shanghai copper in the absence of domestic market-moving news.
Aluminium ended up across the board. August rose 70 to 14,250 yuan per tonne, September 80 to 14,480, October 270 to 14,670, November 150 to 14,750 and December 160 to 14,720 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 5,510 tonnes from 980 tonnes.
